  <div class="sqs-html-content" data-sqsp-text-block-content><p class="sqsrte-small" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Formed in the late ’90s in Washington, DC, Faraquet began as a low-key side project but quickly gained momentum, becoming an incubator for a group of three friends eager to create something unique.</p><p class="sqsrte-small" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Over the next few years, they crafted a sound that fused diverse influences, marked by dynamic shifts, intricate melodies, and a dedication to pushing the boundaries of traditional rock structures. Though their time together was brief, Faraquet left a lasting impact on the indie and progressive rock scenes.</p><p class="sqsrte-small" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">In 2025, the band celebrated the 25th anniversary of their lone LP, The View From This Tower, released by Dischord Records. While initially somewhat overlooked, the album has since become a touchstone of ’90s experimental rock. To mark the occasion, Devin Ocampo, Jeff Boswell, and Chad Molter reunited in July 2025 for their first live performances since 2008.<br><br>Now, due popular demand, they’re coming to London for two special dates!</p></div>

  <div class="sqs-html-content" data-sqsp-text-block-content><p class="sqsrte-small" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Seminal US indie-emo outfit Braid at The Dome this July!</p><p class="sqsrte-small" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">The band haven't visited UK shores in 13 YEARS, and we're stoked to host their long-awaited return to London.&nbsp;</p><p class="sqsrte-small" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">The revered Illinois band are widely considereda pillar of second-wave emo, along with similarly influential acts like the Get Up Kids, the Promise Ring and Jimmy Eat World.&nbsp; Having recently celebrated 25 years of their seminal 1997 album <em>Frame &amp; Canvas</em>, Braid remain a vital, restless force in the indie rock scene, their influence echoing loudly as ever.</p><p class="sqsrte-small" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Could you really think of a better band to join them than Hey Mercedes? The band that 3/4s of Braid created following their dissolution in 1999? You could not, and that’s a fact. Hey Mercedes released an EP on Polyvinyl and two albums on Vagrant, playing 359 shows to wide acclaim before they disbanded in 2005 without ever playing the UK. So here we have it, 20 years after they split, we have a London debut. That’s worth the entry price alone.</p></div>

  <div class="sqs-html-content" data-sqsp-text-block-content><p class="sqsrte-small" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Sigh were formed in April of 1990 and&nbsp;did two demos before the 'Requiem for Fools' 7"EP on Wild Rags, which&nbsp;led them to sign to Euronymous' Deathlike Silence Productions.<br>The debut album<strong><em> 'Scorn Defeat'</em></strong> was recorded in 1993 by Mirai Kawashima (Ba, Vo), Satoshi Fujinami (Dr) and Shinichi Ishikawa (G), but Euronoymous&nbsp;was murdered before its release, and Voices of&nbsp;Wonder Records took over DSP and released <strong><em>'Scorn Defeat.'</em></strong></p><p class="sqsrte-small" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Sigh then moved to Cacophonous Records and released 4 albums, ‘<strong><em>Infidel Art’ </em></strong>&nbsp;(1995), ‘<strong><em>Ghastly Funeral Theatre’</em></strong> (1996 mini album), ‘<strong><em>Hail Horror Hail’</em></strong> (1997) and ‘<strong><em>Scenario IV: Dread Dreams’</em></strong> (1999).</p><p class="sqsrte-small" style="white-space:pre-wrap;"><strong><em>'Hail Horror Hail'</em></strong> was chosen as one of the most important 100 heavy metal albums of the nineties in UK’s Terrorizer Magazine.&nbsp;</p><p class="sqsrte-small" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Sigh then signed to Century Media Records and released<strong><em> 'Imaginary Sonicscape'</em></strong> in 2001. The album was again well received worldwide.&nbsp;</p><p class="sqsrte-small" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Sigh have experienced lots of US/ Europe tours including the festival appearances such as Hellfest (France), Graspop Metal Meeting (Belgium), Brutal Assault Open Air (Czech Republic), Roadburn Festival (Holland), Hammer Open Air Festival (Finland), Damnation Festival (UK), Inferno Festival (Norway), Under the Black Sun (Germany, headliner), Metal Magic Festival (Denmark, headliner), Maryland Deathfest (USA) and many more. Their show is truly theatrical and spectacular with lots of fire and blood.&nbsp;</p><p class="sqsrte-small" data-rte-preserve-empty="true" style="white-space:pre-wrap;"></p></div>

  <div class="sqs-html-content" data-sqsp-text-block-content><p class="sqsrte-small" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Greetings from Suffocate City, The Funeral Portrait’s first full-length for Better Noise Music, expands the group’s mythology to new heights and dimensions with invigorating, authentic, and passionate anthems. Songs like “Alien,” “Voodoo Doll,” “You’re So Ugly When You Cry” (featuring The Used’s Bert McCracken), and the title track (featuring Spencer Charnas of Ice Nine Kills) fuse the vibrant accessibility of Active Rock with the earnest honesty once screamed at the Warped Tour of the 2000s. </p><p class="sqsrte-small" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Steadily growing since the band’s formation in 2014, The Coffin Crew is a worldwide assemblage of devotees united in the shared catharsis of The Funeral Portrait’s music. It’s a tight-knit fandom built in the spirit of AFI’s Despair Faction, the MCRmy, the BVB Army, and Ice Nine Kills’ Psychos. It’s a diverse and welcoming community bound by perseverance through adversity and heartbreak.</p><p class="sqsrte-small" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Heralded as “the inspiring antidote to stagnant metalcore” by Alternative Press early into their career, the band eventually made their way onto SiriusXM Octane and episodes of All Elite Wrestling.</p></div>

Developing an effective, muddy, emo, hardcore post-grunge sound, the band released the I Just Want to Be Pure EP in 2008, following it up with several EPs and full-length releases including, Separation, The Things We Think We’re Missing and Light We Made, with each record introducing new sonic elements to their world.</p><p class="sqsrte-small" style="white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">After their farewell tour in 2019, the band’s 2024 LP <em>With You In Spirit</em> marked a thrilling return to form. This momentum surged through 2025 with a string of new singles, setting the stage for an extensive 2026 global tour across Europe, Latin America, and the UK.</p></div>

  <div class="sqs-html-content" data-sqsp-text-block-content><p class="sqsrte-small" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Agriculture’s formation mirrors their duality. What began as a loose collaboration between Kern Haug and Dan Meyer in the Los Angeles noise scene evolved into a shared pursuit of the sublime through heavy music. With the additions of Richard Chowenhill and Leah Levinson, the project solidified into the band’s current form. The ecstatic black metal foundation that was laid on 2022’s The Circle Chant expanded into something more precise and far-reaching on their 2023 self-titled full-length, and deepened further with 2024’s Living Is Easy: a record that embraced devotional intensity and radiant heaviness in equal measure.</p><p class="sqsrte-small" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Agriculture’s writing process is built on dismantling and revision of self. Dan and Leah bring songs to the band and then allow them to be pulled apart and rebuilt communally: reshaped through conflict, repetition, and deep trust. Richard adds guitar melodies and solos, and Kern constructs rhythms which are sometimes familiar but often unconventional. Finally, with Richard producing, the final form of each song is realised through intense collaborative work in the studio. Although a time consuming and ego-frustrating process, this allows the band to find the spirit of the songs not through inspiration, but through persistence.</p></div>

  <div class="sqs-html-content" data-sqsp-text-block-content><p class="sqsrte-small" style="text-align: center; ; white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true"><strong>Born Again Concerts proudly presents 25 year anniversary European summer tour 2026 I KILLED THE PROM QUEEN with very special guests LONG GOODBYE and ETERNAL LORD live at The Dome</strong></p><p class="sqsrte-small" style="text-align: start; ; white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">I Killed The Prom Queen are an Australian Metalcore band from Adelaide, formed in 2001. They were prominent in the Australian live music scene and toured the US, Japan and Europe several times. They issued three studio albums: When Goodbye Means Forever... (2003), Music for the Recently Deceased (2006) and Beloved (2014). The latter two albums peaked at #27 and #6 on the ARIA Albums Chart respectively.</p><p class="sqsrte-small" style="text-align: start; ; white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">The band initially split up in April 2007 due to the inability to find a permanent vocalist. They reformed with vocalist Michael Crafter to play a farewell tour in mid-2008 and released a live album and DVD, Sleepless Nights and City Lights, which peaked at #48 in Australia. In May 2011 the band reformed with new vocalist Jamie Hope and performed on the Destroy Music Tour. They subsequently released their third studio album Beloved in February 2014.</p><p class="sqsrte-small" style="text-align: start; ; white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">On 10 April 2025, the band announced their 25th Anniversary Tour to take place in October, in which they will only play songs between 2000 and 2008. Emmure, To The Grave, and Threshold were announced as support. </p><p class="sqsrte-small" style="text-align: start; ; white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true"><strong>A statement from Anotations Of An Autopsy </strong></p><p class="sqsrte-small" style="text-align: start; ; white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true"><em>“Hello everyone, unfortunately we will no longer be playing the two UK dates of the I Killed The Prom Queen European tour.&nbsp;Instead, we are focusing on remaining in the studio and working on album number 3.<br>We would like to sincerely apologise to anyone who bought a ticket with the intent to see us at these shows, We promise that we will make it up to you all in the future.<br>The shows are still going ahead without us so please show up and give this great line up some love!<br><br>We look forward to seeing you all later in the year.&nbsp;</em></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: start; ; white-space:pre-wrap;" data-rte-preserve-empty="true"><em>AOAA”</em></p></div>

  <div class="sqs-html-content" data-sqsp-text-block-content><p class="sqsrte-small" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Washington, D.C.'s Periphery push at the boundaries of progressive metal, utilising detuned, extended-range instruments to create a sound that's as technically dizzying as it is relentlessly heavy. Using a framework laid down by djent pioneers like <a href="https://open.spotify.com/artist/3ggwAqZD3lyT2sbovlmfQY">Meshuggah</a> and running wild with it, the group issued an eponymous debut in 2010. Periphery hit their stride with the double-LP Juggernaut (2015) and the diverse Periphery III: Select Difficulty (2016), the latter of which earned them a Grammy nomination for Best Metal Performance. The band elicited accolades on subsequent efforts, Periphery IV: Hail Stan (2019) and Periphery V: Djent Is Not a Genre (2023), for their commitment to innovation and experimentation.</p></div>

  <div class="sqs-html-content" data-sqsp-text-block-content><p class="sqsrte-small" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Starbenders are a rock-n-roll dream come true for every hard luck dreamer occupying this third stone from the sun. Singer/songwriter Kimi Shelter is the love child Johnny Thunders and Joan Jett should have had, raised with an impeccable education from Blondie Elementary School, Def Leppard High, Bowie College, and a Ph.D from Siouxie Sioux University in Fuck All Y’all. Aaron Lecesne brings ripping bass lines, vivid musicality, fashionista chic, and lightning rod stage energy. Kriss Tokaji is the literal embodiment of a Guitar Adonis whose fretboard mastery easily places him at the pinnacle of today’s young guns, a legend in the making. This band has toured the world with everyone from Alice In Chains to Palaye Royale, destroying the entire house every time. They’ve issued twenty-six releases in eight years - singles, EPs, and LPs, including their 2020 full-length, Love Potions, for Sumerian Records. Another album’s worth of new material is currently awaiting release. With a work ethic as relentless as their fabulous vision, there is much more magic yet to come.</p></div>

  <div class="sqs-html-content" data-sqsp-text-block-content><p class="sqsrte-small" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Corrosion of Conformity (also known as C.O.C.), was founded in North Carolina by guitarist Woody Weatherman in the early 1980s as one of the first punk metal fusion bands. C.O.C. were known in their early years for their aggressive sound, their clever political lyrics and their willingness to turn away from hardcore and metal conventions. Their shift to a more essential and reduced sound (kind of a deep-South Black Sabbath) in the 1990s brought them closer to the alternative metal zeitgeist and gave them some favors within the mainstream scene.&nbsp;</p></div>

  <div class="sqs-html-content" data-sqsp-text-block-content><p class="sqsrte-small" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Liquids are inherently fluid, just like skaiwater, an artist who can’t be contained by any category, whether that’s genre, gender identity, or just their open-ended approach to life. The gentle AutoTune layered across their vocals isn’t a mask, but a way of expressing the deeper levels of their voice beyond what you might hear on a phone call: skaiwater’s register isn’t high or low, but somehow both at the same time.</p><p style="text-align:justify;white-space: normal !important;white-space:pre-wrap;" class="sqsrte-small">The UK-born, LA-based polymath continues to expand their sonic universe, most recently with their independent 2026 album <em>Wonderful</em>, a self-directed exploration of modern chaos, social influence, and cultural conspiracies. Following the critical acclaim of <em>#gigi</em>, which was an awakening and only the beginning of the endless possibilities for an artist who lets themselves follow whatever wave feels right, skaiwater has cemented themselves as a force in music.</p><p style="text-align:justify;white-space: normal !important;white-space:pre-wrap;" class="sqsrte-small">As both a behind-the-scenes producer and a direct artistic collaborator, skaiwater has worked with a spectrum of artists across the pop landscape—from Lil Nas X to Lil Uzi Vert to Lil Keed, from Skepta to PinkPantheress. skaiwater can go bar-for-bar with the best of them but is just as capable of softening themselves to express a deeper vulnerability. They’ve taken everything learned from these creative relationships and honed their own authentic voice.</p><p style="text-align:justify;white-space: normal !important;white-space:pre-wrap;" class="sqsrte-small">Building on this momentum, skaiwater has toured with BKThaRula, appeared on PinkPantheress’ North American tour, performed at Rolling Loud, and most recently featured on K-Pop girl group I-DLE’s single “Mono,” which has amassed over 20 million views on YouTube.</p><p style="text-align:justify;white-space: normal !important;white-space:pre-wrap;" class="sqsrte-small">Fluidity also defines their embrace of remixing, whether in their own experiments or by letting collaborators explore untapped potential in their work. There are infinite versions of skaiwater’s songs because there are infinite versions of skaiwater’s selves, and none of them cancel each other out. None of the unexpected musical collisions that come together with skaiwater at the center are opposites, because what unites them all is skaiwater’s genuine love of not just making music, but existing. And what is music but purely existing? skaiwater is making waves, not just in the industry, but with sound itself, much like the tides.</p></div>

  <div class="sqs-html-content" data-sqsp-text-block-content><p class="sqsrte-small" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Born from the industrial grit of Elizabeth, New Jersey, E-Town Concrete didn’t just blur the lines between hardcore and hip-hop-they blazed a path that many of today's bands are still following.Formed in the late-’90s, E-Town Concrete pioneered a sound that fused metallic hardcore aggression with hip-hop groove, streetwise lyricism, and undeniable bounce. Long before“crossover” became algorithm-friendly or festival-programmed, E-Town was packing rooms with a style that felt equally at home in underground VFW halls and blasting through car speakers acrossDirty Jerz. Their landmark release The Renaissance (2003) produced anthems like “Mandibles,” “Baptism,”and “So Many Nights”-records that became generational rallying cries and social media memes for hardcore tastemakers. But what once felt ahead of its time now feels prophetic.Over the last several years, a new wave of hardcore bands has exploded-many leaning heavily into the exact fusion of groove-driven riffs, hip-hop cadence, and rhythmic mosh that E-Town established decades ago. From the bounce in modern hardcore breakdowns to the swagger in vocal delivery, the influence is unmistakable.</p></div>

  <div class="sqs-html-content" data-sqsp-text-block-content><p class="sqsrte-small" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Way Dynamic, the solo project of Melbourne’s Dylan Young, released Massive Shoe in 2025 – a third album that’s playful and understated, luminous and textured. Massive Shoe is minimalist folk-pop, art rock and baroque pop, produced and largely played by Young, who moonlights in Melbourne’s beloved Cool Sounds and Good Morning and has played drums with Snowy Band and Kankawa Nagarra. With upcoming shows supporting Black Country, New Road and This is Lorelei, 2026 already looks busy.</p><p class="sqsrte-small" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">It’s tempting to only compare these timeless songs to those of yesteryear, but there’s a sensibility, a turn of phrase, that feels deeply contemporary: it’s telling that Waxahatchee’s Katie Crutchfield described “Miffed It” as her “favourite song in a VERY long time”, and Katie and MJ Lenderman have both taken Way Dynamic on tour. At the same time, Sir Elton John said that he “just cannot stop listening” to “Ibiza”. Young’s songs don’t shy away from sentiment, or equally from silliness: on any given song he might evoke a cruisy trip through hell or earnestly lament a miscommunication. Whether the journey is to space or along the Seine, we’re very much along for the ride.</p></div>

  <div class="sqs-html-content" data-sqsp-text-block-content><p class="sqsrte-small" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Friendship, the Philly-based band of Dan Wriggins, Michael Cormier-O’Leary, Jon Samuels, and Peter Gill, has roots tracing back to Yarmouth, Maine, the small town where Wriggins, Gill, and Cormier-O’Leary grew up-- taking their name from Friendship, Maine, about an hour up the coast. They moved to Philly in 2015, and the Friendship band has expanded and contracted ever since.</p><p class="sqsrte-small" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Caveman Wakes Up (2025) is an album for sleeping and waking, walking and driving, hunting and fishing, for loitering outside a roadhouse on the haunted tundra. Okay in elevators, not great for dinner. On Caveman Wakes Up, the band’s historically capacious definition of country music grows wider still. Shambolic guitars are offset by flute pads, bleary poetry is set against a Motown rhythm section, a song about Jerry Garcia and First Lady Betty Ford fades out with a drum solo, like if Talk Talk came from a dingy Philadelphia basement and was fronted by James Tate. Wriggins’ ragged baritone cuts through eleven murky, swirling country-rock songs with profound lyrical substance and sincerity. Like an alarm clock incorporated into the edge of a dream, Caveman Wakes Up belongs equally to the conscious and subconscious mind, fraught with background, steeped in reference and experimentation, delivered casually and as a dire warning, dedicated, above all, to music’s creative soul.</p></div>
